wire_profiles.limits: Six scalar types plus NULL; signed values vary by row, binary covers all 256 byte values. Includes scalar validation, formatting, framed-row construction and allocator work. Reuses each backend buffer; output escapes optimization. Excludes metadata, TLS, sockets, authority and storage. Framed bytes are database-protocol application bytes, not network traffic. Local observations, not a throughput or latency guarantee.

Native includes a fresh process and compilation; drivers retain a connection and prepared handles. Sequential local observations include authority and TLS costs; other proof/build tasks may compete for resources. No throughput, speedup or production latency claim.

Connect includes verified TLS, authentication and driver startup. Preparation excludes execution. First-row/complete use raw PostgreSQL frames and unbuffered Connector/Python, including driver and transport work. Writes include durable admission and observed completion. RSS is a Linux process sample; HWM covers this activation, not an allocator bound. Timings are sequential local observations, not an SLO or an encoding-only benchmark.

One cold preparation/read per path through a bounded HTTP diagnostic proxy; this changes transport costs and is separate from unproxied timings. Counts cover gateway and explicit native caller attempts during each wall-clock window, including concurrent account maintenance; Catalog worker/courier requests bypass the proxy. Provider and authority work come from completed x-transit-work responses. Byte counters are native JSON payloads, not TLS/database-wire traffic. No payloads or credentials are retained; no causal subtraction or speedup claim.

public_sdk_interop.limits: Local consumer installation and ten counter/query pairs. Excludes artifact builds, CI setup/cache transfer, and other SDK failure suites. Not a hosted CI budget measurement.
